src: 2 · Four tones and the neutral tone
Hear and say the four tones and the neutral tone, and tell apart words that differ only in tone.
mom
numb; hemp
horse
to scold
to buy
to sell
soup
sugar
mom
very fast
Which tone is low, and dips when said alone?
The first tone
The second tone
The third tone
The fourth tone
The third tone (ǎ) is low; alone it dips and comes back up.
A word with the fourth tone comes at the end of your question. What happens to its tone?
It still falls
It rises, as in an English question
It becomes the first tone
It loses its tone
The tone belongs to the word, so it falls even at the end of a question.
买 (mǎi) and 卖 (mài) differ only in tone. What do they mean?
to sell and to buy
to buy and to sell
to buy and a buyer
the same thing
买 with the third tone is to buy; 卖 with the fourth tone is to sell.
Which tone mark shows a falling tone?
The fourth tone mark (à) points down: the voice falls.
Which word is mǎi (to buy)?
买 is mǎi; 卖 (mài) is to sell.
Which is the pinyin of 糖 (sugar)?
糖 rises: táng. tāng, with a level tone, is soup.
In 妈妈 (mom), which tone does the second 妈 have?
The neutral tone
The first tone
The third tone
The fourth tone
The second syllable of 妈妈 is short and light: it has no tone mark.
What does 马 (mǎ) mean?
horse
mom
to scold
numb
马 with the third tone is horse; mā is mom and mà is to scold.
买马 (to buy a horse) in pinyin
买 (mǎi) has the third tone; mài, with the fourth tone, means to sell.
妈妈 (mom) in pinyin, one syllable per tile
The first 妈 has the first tone; the second has the neutral tone, with no mark.
很快 (very fast) in pinyin
A tone pair: the third tone on hěn, then the fourth tone on kuài.
horse
马 has the third tone: mǎ. mā is mom and mà is to scold.
soup
汤 has the first tone, high and level: tāng. táng is sugar.
to sell
卖 has the fourth tone: mài. mǎi would be to buy.
Type the pinyin of 卖 (to sell)
fourth tone · use the accent bar
卖 has the fourth tone: it falls. mǎi is to buy.
Type the pinyin of 糖 (sugar)
second tone · use the accent bar
糖 has the second tone: it rises. tāng is soup.
Type the pinyin of 妈 (mom)
first tone · use the accent bar
妈 has the first tone: high and level. mǎ is horse.
3 · Tone changes: 不, 一, third tone
Say 不 and 一 with the right tone, and say two third tones in a row the way Chinese speakers do.
is not; no
you're welcome
not good
one person
one day
first
hello
very good
How do you say 不 in 不是 (is not)?
bù, falling
bú, rising
bū, high and level
with no tone
不 before a fourth tone (shì) rises: bú shì.
Two third tones come in a row, as in 你好. How are they said?
Both low and dipping
Both falling
The first one like a second tone
The second one like a second tone
The first of two third tones is said like a second tone: 你好 sounds like ní hǎo.
In which of these is 一 said yī, with the first tone?
第一 (first)
一个人 (one person)
一天 (one day)
一起 (together)
After 第 and in counting, 一 keeps its first tone; before a word it changes.
Which is the pinyin of 不是 (is not)?
不 before a fourth tone rises: bú shì.
How do Chinese speakers say 你好 (hello)?
ní hǎo, with the first syllable rising
nǐ hǎo, with two full dips
nǐ hào, with the second syllable falling
nì hǎo, with the first syllable falling
The first of two third tones is said like a second tone; the pinyin still writes nǐ hǎo.
Which is the pinyin of 一个人 (one person)?
个 counts as a fourth tone, so 一 before it rises: yí ge.
In which phrase is 不 said bù, with its fourth tone?
Before a third tone (hǎo) 不 keeps its fourth tone: bù hǎo.
When does 一 keep its first tone, yī?
When you count: yī, èr, sān
Before a fourth tone
Before 个
Before a first tone
In counting, at the end of a bigger number (十一) and after 第, 一 stays yī.
不是 (is not) in pinyin
Tone change: 不 before a fourth tone is bú.
一个人 (one person) in pinyin
一 before 个 takes the second tone: yí ge rén.
不好 (not good) in pinyin
Before a third tone, 不 keeps its fourth tone: bù hǎo.
you're welcome
客 has the fourth tone, so 不 rises: bú kèqi.
together
Before a third tone (qǐ), 一 is said yì: yìqǐ.
first
After 第, 一 keeps its first tone: dìyī.
Type the pinyin of 不客气 (you're welcome)
two words · 不 changes before a fourth tone
Tone change: 不 before a fourth tone is bú, so bú kèqi.
one person (in characters)
个 goes between the number and the noun
A number needs a measure word before the noun: 一个人.
Type the pinyin of 你好 (hello), the way it is written
two words · pinyin writes the dictionary tones
Pinyin writes the third tone mark on both: nǐ hǎo, though you say ní hǎo.
4 · How characters work: strokes and radicals
Recognize about 25 basic characters and see how pictures, compounds and radicals build the rest.
person
tree; wood
mountain
woods
bright
good
What is a radical?
A part of a character that hints at its meaning
A letter of the Chinese alphabet
The pinyin of a character
A tone mark
A radical, such as 氵 for water, hints at the meaning; it does not spell the sound.
What does 休 (to rest) show?
Two trees
A person leaning on a tree
The sun and the moon
An open mouth
休 is 亻 (person) next to 木 (tree): someone resting against a tree.
Which characters does this course teach?
Traditional characters, as in Taiwan
A mix of both
Simplified characters, as in mainland China
Pinyin only, no characters
The course teaches simplified characters, used in mainland China, with pinyin under them.
Which character began as a picture of a tree?
木 is a tree with its roots; two of them make 林, woods.
好 (good) is made of 女 and 子. What do they mean?
woman and child
sun and moon
person and tree
mouth and water
女 is woman and 子 is child: together, good.
Which part of 汤 (soup) hints at its meaning?
氵 on the left, which means water
The right side, which spells the sound
Its top stroke
No part: characters give no hints
Three dots on the left (氵) mark words to do with water.
Which is the pinyin of 好 (good)?
好 (good) has the third tone: hǎo.
明 (bright) is 日 + 月. What are they?
the sun and the moon
two trees
a person and a tree
a mouth and a door
日 is the sun and 月 is the moon: together, bright.
a good person (in characters)
The describer goes before the noun: 好人, good person.
好人 (a good person) in pinyin
好 has the third tone mark: hǎo rén.
a big mountain (in characters; 大 = big)
The describer goes before the noun: 大山, big mountain.
sun + moon = bright
The sun and the moon together make 明, bright.
tree + tree = woods
Two trees make 林 (woods); three trees make 森 (forest).
woman + child = good
女 (woman) and 子 (child) make 好, good.
Type the pinyin of 好 (good)
third tone · use the accent bar
好 has the third tone mark: hǎo.
a good person (in characters)
the describer comes first
The describer goes before the noun: 好人.
Type the pinyin of 人 (person)
second tone · use the accent bar
人 has the second tone: it rises, rén.
5 · Hello, thank you, sorry: Chinese courtesy
Say hello, thank you, sorry and goodbye, give your name, and know when to use the polite 您.
Hello!
Hello! (polite)
Hello, Teacher Wang!
Thank you!
You're welcome.
I'm sorry.
That's OK.
Excuse me, what's your last name?
My last name is Wang.
My name is Wang Ming.
Excuse me! (calling a server)
Goodbye!
When should you use 您 instead of 你?
With your best friend
With an older person, a teacher or a customer
With a small child
Never; it is old-fashioned
您 shows respect: for older people, teachers, and from staff to customers.
What does 你好吗？ usually mean?
Hi! (a casual greeting)
Goodbye
A real question: are you doing well?
Thank you
你好吗 asks how someone really is; for a casual hi, say 你好.
Which word do you use to call a server in a restaurant?
Call a server 服务员; 小姐 now has a bad meaning in mainland China.
Which is the pinyin of 您 (you, polite)?
您 has the second tone: nín. 你 has the third tone: nǐ.
Which do you say to an older neighbor?
您好 is the polite hello for older people.
Someone says 对不起 to you. What do you answer?
没关系 (that's OK) answers an apology; 不客气 answers thanks.
Your friend says 谢谢. What do you answer?
不客气 (you're welcome) answers thanks.
How do you call a server in a restaurant?
服务员 is the normal word; 小姐 suggests a sex worker in the mainland.
您好 (hello, polite) in pinyin
您 has the second tone: it rises, nín hǎo.
a Chinese teacher (a teacher of Chinese)
The describer goes before the noun: 中文老师.
My name is Wang Ming.
叫 means to be called: 我叫 + your name.
My last name is Wang.
Answer with 姓; 贵 is only for the other person's name.
Excuse me, what's your last name?
请问 (may I ask) opens a polite question.
That's OK.
没关系 (that's OK) answers sorry; 不客气 answers thank you.
Type the pinyin of 再见 (goodbye)
fourth tone + fourth tone · one word
再见 is two fourth tones: zàijiàn.
an American teacher (美国 = America)
the describer comes first
The describer goes before the noun: 美国老师.
My last name is Li. (answering 您贵姓？)
Answer with 我姓 + surname; 贵 is only for the person you ask.
6 · Pronouns and 们
Say I, you, he, she, we and they, make them plural with 们, and say my friend or their teacher.
His name is Wang Ming.
Her last name is Li.
Hello, everyone! (to a group)
Hello, everybody!
five students
my friend
My friend's name is Anna.
Our teacher's last name is Wang.
How do you say we?
我s
们 after a pronoun makes it plural: 我们.
How do 他 (he) and 她 (she) sound?
他 is tā, 她 is tà
Exactly the same: tā
她 is said nǚ
他 rises and 她 falls
他, 她 and 它 are all tā; only the character shows the difference.
Which is right for five students?
A number takes a measure word and no 们: 五个学生.
Which is the pinyin of 他 (he)?
他 has the first tone: high and level, tā.
How do you say we?
们 makes 我 plural: 我们.
You hear tā in a sentence. Who is it?
he, she or it: they sound the same
only he
only she
only it
他, 她 and 它 are all tā; context tells you which.
Which is right for three students?
After a number, use 个 and no 们.
Which word means they, for a group of women?
她 + 们 is a group of women; 他们 covers men or mixed groups.
their teacher
The owner goes before the noun: 他们的老师.
five students (五 = five)
A number needs a measure word before the noun, and no 们: 五个学生.
His name is Wang Ming.
叫 gives the full name; 姓 gives only the last name.
Hello, everyone! (to a group of friends)
你 + 们 is you all: 你们好.
five students
A number takes 个 before the noun: 五个学生.
Our teacher's last name is Wang.
我们 is we or us; with 的, our.
five students (五 = five)
no 们 after a number
A number needs a measure word before the noun, and no 们: 五个学生.
my friend
the owner comes first
The owner goes before the noun: 我的朋友, or 我朋友 for a close friend.
Hello, everyone! (to a group)
们 makes you plural: 你们好. 大家好 works too.
7 · 是: A is B
Say who you are and where you are from with 是, and say what you are not with 不是.
I'm American.
She's a teacher.
I'm a student.
He isn't Chinese.
Wang Ming is Chinese.
He's an American student.
Teacher Li is a Chinese teacher.
I'm a student too.
Which sentence means I'm American?
Noun 是 noun: 我是美国人. 美国 alone is the country.
How is 不是 said?
不 before a fourth tone rises: bú shì.
Where does 也 (also) go?
At the end, like too
Before the verb
Before the subject
After the verb
也 goes right before the verb: 我也是学生.
Which is the pinyin of 是 (to be)?
是 has the fourth tone: it falls, shì.
I'm American.
Noun 是 noun, and 美国人 (American person), not 美国 (America).
He isn't a teacher.
不 goes right before 是: 不是.
Which word means a Chinese person?
Country + 人: 中国人. 中文 is the language.
I'm a student too.
也 goes right before 是, not at the end like too.
I'm a student too.
也 goes before the verb, not at the end like English too.
He's an American student. (start with he)
The describer goes before the noun: 美国学生.
She isn't Chinese.
是 is negated with 不, never with 没.
I'm American.
是 joins two nouns: I = American.
He isn't a teacher.
Is not is 不是; 没 never goes with 是.
Wang Ming is Chinese.
Country + 人 is a person from there; 中文 is the language.
I'm a student too.
also goes before 是
也 goes before the verb: 我也是学生.
She's an English teacher. (a teacher of English)
英语 (English) · 老师
The describer goes before the noun: 英语老师.
I'm not American.
Use 不 with 是; 没 never goes with 是.
8 · Adjectives with 很 (no 是)
Describe people and things with 很, 不 and 太…了, without the 是 that English makes you want.
She's tall.
I'm busy.
I'm tired.
I'm fine.
She's tall; I'm not.
I'm not busy.
The coffee isn't expensive.
That's too expensive!
Great!
He's a good friend.
a very good friend
Which sentence means He's tall?
Adjectives work like verbs: no 是, and 很 goes before the adjective.
What does 很 add in 我很好 (I'm fine)?
Usually little: it is glue before the adjective
Always a strong very
It turns it into a question
It shows the past
In a plain statement 很 mostly makes the sentence sound complete.
How do you say not busy?
不 goes right before the adjective, with no 是: 不忙.
Which is the pinyin of 很 (very)?
很 has the third tone: low, hěn.
She's tall.
No 是 before an adjective; use 很.
I'm not busy.
不 goes right before the adjective, with no 是.
That's too expensive!
Too is 太 + adjective + 了.
a good friend
The adjective goes before the noun; with 很 you would need 的.
He's tall.
很 goes before the verb, and an adjective works like a verb: 他很高, no 是.
a good friend
The describer goes before the noun: 好朋友.
That's too expensive!
Too is 太 + adjective + 了, with no 是.
I'm tired.
Adjectives take 很, not 是: 我很累.
The coffee isn't expensive.
Put 不 right before the adjective: 不贵.
That's too expensive!
太 … 了 means too: 太贵了.
I'm very busy.
no 是
很 goes before the verb, and 忙 works like a verb: 我很忙, no 是.
a good friend
the describer comes first
The describer goes before the noun: 好朋友.
She isn't tall. (use 不 + adjective)
不 goes right before the adjective, with no 是.
9 · Questions with 吗 and 呢
Ask yes/no questions with 吗, answer them the Chinese way, and ask back with 你呢.
Are you a teacher?
Are you busy?
Are you a student too?
Yes, I'm a teacher.
Are you Chinese?
No, I'm American.
No, I'm not busy.
I'm fine. And you?
How do you turn 你是老师。 into a question?
Raise your voice at the end
Add 吗 at the end
Put 是 first
Add 呢 at the start
Keep the statement and add 吗: 你是老师吗？
你是学生吗？ How do you say yes?
是。 or 是，我是学生。
Answer with the verb from the question: 是.
What does 你呢？ do?
It says goodbye
It asks the other person's name
It asks the same question back
It says no
呢 after a person sends the question back: and you?
Which is the pinyin of 吗?
ma, with no tone mark
吗 has the neutral tone: short and light, with no mark.
Are you a teacher?
Keep the statement and add 吗 at the end.
你忙吗？ Answer: Yes, I am.
Answer with the adjective: 很忙. An adjective never takes 是.
你是中国人吗？ Answer: No.
Answer with the verb from the question: 不是.
我很好，你呢？ What does 你呢 mean here?
And you?
Are you?
Who are you?
Goodbye.
呢 sends the question back: and you?
Are you a student too?
也 goes before the verb: 你也是学生吗？
Is he an American student? (start with he)
The describer goes before the noun: 美国学生, then 吗 at the end.
Are you busy?
No 是 before an adjective; 吗 at the end asks the question.
Are you American?
吗 at the end turns a statement into a yes/no question.
I'm busy. And you?
呢 after a person asks the same question back.
Are you busy? I'm not.
Answer with the adjective itself: 不忙.
Are you going tomorrow? (明天 = tomorrow, 去 = go)
the time word comes before 去
Time goes before the verb: 你明天去吗？
Is she a teacher too?
也 goes before the verb: 她也是老师吗？
Are you a teacher?
Add 吗 to the statement to ask a yes/no question.
10 · Question words: 什么, 谁, 哪儿, 几
Ask what, who, where, which country and how many, keeping the Chinese word order.
What's your name?
Who is he?
He's my friend.
Where do you live?
Excuse me, where do you work?
What country are you from?
How many older brothers do you have?
Where does a question word go in a Chinese question?
Always first, as in English
Where the answer would go
Always last
After 吗
Put the question word where the answer goes: 你住哪儿？ 我住纽约.
Is 你叫什么名字吗？ correct?
Yes, it is more polite
Yes, 吗 is always needed
No: 什么 must come first
No: a question word already asks, so drop 吗
Question words never take 吗: 你叫什么名字？
How do you ask someone's nationality?
哪 (which) + 国人: 你是哪国人？
Which is the pinyin of 几 (how many)?
几 has the third tone: low, jǐ.
What's your name?
什么 stays where the answer goes, and no 吗.
Who is he?
谁 goes where the answer would be: 他是我朋友 → 他是谁？
Where do you live?
哪儿 goes after 住, where the place goes in the answer.
Which question is correct?
哪国人 stays where the answer goes, with no 吗.
Where do you work? (在 = at, 工作 = to work)
Where it happens comes before the verb: 你在哪儿工作？
How many older brothers do you have? (哥哥 = older brother)
几 needs a measure word before the noun: 几个哥哥.
What's your name?
什么 stays where the answer goes, and a question word takes no 吗.
Who is he?
谁 asks who; it goes where the answer would be.
Where do you live?
哪儿 asks where.
What country are you from?
哪国人 asks which country someone is from.
Where do you work? (在 = at, 工作 = to work)
where comes first
Where it happens goes before the verb: 你在哪儿工作？
How many older brothers do you have? (哥哥 = older brother)
几 takes a measure word before the noun: 几个哥哥.
What's your name? (to a friend)
no 吗
The question word stays where the answer goes, with no 吗.
11 · Negation: 不 and 没 (not, didn't)
Say what you don't do, what you don't have, and what didn't happen, with the right word for "not".
I don't drink (alcohol).
She isn't busy.
I'm not going tomorrow.
I don't have any money.
I don't have money. (casual)
I didn't go yesterday.
He didn't eat. / He hasn't eaten.
I'm not a teacher.
How do you say "I don't have a phone"?
有 is negated only with 没: 没有.
How do you say "I didn't go yesterday"?
没 for an action that did not happen, before the verb, with no 了.
"I don't drink coffee" is a habit. Which is right?
A habit takes 不, right before the verb; 我没喝咖啡 means "I didn't drink coffee".
Which is the pinyin of 不是 (is not)?
Tone change: 不 before a fourth tone takes the second tone, bú shì.
'I don't have money' =
有 is the one verb that takes 没, never 不.
'He didn't eat' =
An action that did not happen takes 没, and no 了 after 没.
'I'm not busy' =
A state takes 不, right before the adjective, with no 是.
'He doesn't like coffee' =
Liking is a state, so it takes 不: 他不喜欢咖啡.
He didn't come yesterday (start with 他)
The time word and 没 both go before the verb, and 没 never takes 了.
I don't drink tea
A habit takes 不, and 不 goes before the verb: 我不喝茶.
She doesn't have a phone
有 is negated with 没, never with 不.
I don't have money.
Only 没 negates 有: 没有.
I didn't go yesterday.
Yesterday's action did not happen, so 没.
I don't drink alcohol.
A habit or a choice takes 不.
I'm not going tomorrow.
明天 (tomorrow) · 去 · a plan takes 不
Tomorrow and 不 both go before the verb: 我明天不去.
I didn't go yesterday.
昨天 (yesterday) · 去
Yesterday and 没 go before the verb, and 没 takes no 了: 我昨天没去.
I don't have a phone.
手机 (phone)
有 is negated only with 没: 我没有手机.
12 · 的: possession and describing
Say whose something is and what it is like, with the owner or the describer before the noun.
This is my book.
The teacher's phone is expensive.
I like red cars.
These are very expensive clothes.
He's my good friend.
My mom is a teacher.
She's my friend.
How do you say "the book of my teacher"?
The owner goes first, then 的, then the thing: 我老师的书.
A friend says 我妈妈 (my mom). What is missing, and is that OK?
是; it's a mistake
的; it's a mistake
们; it's fine
的; it's fine with family words
With family and close relationships, 的 usually drops after a pronoun.
How do you say "a red car"?
The describer goes in front of the noun, joined by 的.
Which is the pinyin of 书 (book)?
书 has the first tone: high and level.
'my friend' =
The owner comes first, then 的, then the noun.
'the teacher's phone' =
Owner + 的 + thing, like English 's.
'my mom' (the most natural way) =
Family words usually drop 的 after a pronoun: 我妈妈.
'very expensive clothes' =
A describer with 很 needs 的, and it goes in front of the noun.
my teacher's book
The owner goes before the noun, joined by 的: 我老师的书.
a red car
The describer goes before the noun: 红色的车.
This is my mom's phone
Owner, then 的, then the thing: the owner goes before the noun.
This is my book.
的 joins the owner to the thing: 我的书.
She's my good friend.
A one-syllable adjective can join the noun directly: 好朋友.
The teacher's phone is expensive.
Owner + 的 + thing: 老师的手机.
my Chinese teacher
the describers come first
Both describers go before the noun: 我的中文老师.
a very expensive car
车 (car)
A describer with 很 goes before the noun, joined by 的: 很贵的车.
My mom doesn't have a phone.
Family words need no 的, and 有 is negated with 没: 我妈妈没有手机.
13 · 有: have and there is
Say what you have, ask a shop if it has something, and say what there is in a place.
I have a phone.
Do you have coffee?
Is there a bank nearby?
There's a book on the table.
There's no supermarket nearby.
I don't have a car.
The book is on the table.
"There's a bank nearby." Where does 附近 (nearby) go?
At the start, before 有
At the end, after 银行
Between 有 and 银行
Nowhere: Chinese doesn't need it
The place comes first, then 有: 附近有银行.
What does 附近没有银行 mean?
There's a bank nearby.
Is there a bank nearby?
There's no bank nearby.
I don't have a bank.
没有 after a place means "there isn't".
What can 有 mean?
to be (am, is, are)
at, in
to want
to have, and there is
有 covers both "have" and "there is".
Which is the pinyin of 买 (to buy)?
买 has the third tone; mài with the fourth tone is 卖, to sell.
'I have a phone' =
Person + 有 + thing, as in English.
'There's no supermarket nearby' =
Place first, then 没有; 有 never takes 不.
'There's a book on the table' =
Chinese starts with the place, then 有, then number + measure word + noun.
